question: Flexibility in plants is due to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**collenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Collenchyma** is a specialized plant tissue that provides flexible support to plant organs, allowing for growth and movement.
 
• It is typically found in regions of primary growth, such as stems, leaves, and petioles.
 
• Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened walls, which contribute to their ability to provide mechanical support while still allowing for flexibility.
 
• This tissue is particularly abundant in parts of plants that are subject to bending and swaying, such as the edges of leaves and young stems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sclerenchyma**:

 
 
• This tissue provides rigid support and strength to plants but lacks the flexibility of collenchyma.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified walls and are often dead at maturity.
 
• Commonly found in seed coats, nutshells, and fibers.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma**:
 
 
• These are the most common plant cells, involved in photosynthesis, storage, and tissue repair.
 
• Parenchyma cells have thin walls and are alive at maturity.
 
• They are found throughout the plant body.
 
 
 
• **Cambium**:
 
 
• This is a type of meristematic tissue responsible for secondary growth in plants.
 
• It forms new layers of vascular tissue, increasing the thickness of stems and roots.
